How to Keep a Clean Home With Pets: Pet Hair, Odors and Pet-Safe Products

Pets make a house a home, and they bring hair, odors and muddy paws with them. Here's how to keep up, room by room, with products that are safe for your pets.

Get My Instant QuoteCall (469) 210-8005

Published 2026-10-20 · Salt of the Earth Cleaning Co.

We love a home with a dog snoozing on the rug or a cat watching from the window. We also know what comes with them: hair on the couch, nose prints on the glass door, a litter box that needs constant attention and paw prints after every rainy walk.

A clean home with pets isn't about perfection. It's about a few smart habits, the right tools and products you don't have to worry about. Here's what works.

Getting ahead of pet hair

For most pet owners, hair is the biggest everyday challenge. The trick is to catch it before it settles into carpets, furniture and corners.

Brush your pets often

The more hair you brush off outside or in one spot, the less ends up on your floors. During shedding season in spring and fall, a few extra brushing sessions make a noticeable difference.

Vacuum on a schedule

Hair builds up faster than most people expect. Vacuum high-traffic areas, pet beds and the spots your pets love most a few times a week. A vacuum with a pet attachment or a motorized brush head helps pull hair out of carpet fibers.

Don't forget edges and corners

Pet hair drifts. It collects along baseboards, under furniture, in vent covers and in the corners of stairs. Use a crevice tool along edges and wipe baseboards with a damp cloth so hair doesn't just move around.

Tackle upholstery

A rubber glove or a damp rubber squeegee is surprisingly good at lifting hair from couches and chairs. Run it in one direction and the hair balls right up. Washable throws on your pet's favorite spot make cleanup even easier.

Controlling pet odors

Odors usually come from a few predictable places. Find the source and you're most of the way there.

  • Pet bedding. Wash beds, blankets and covers regularly. Odors build up in fabric long before you notice them.
  • Litter boxes. Scoop daily and refresh the litter on a regular schedule. Wipe the area around the box, where litter scatters.
  • Food and water bowls. Wash them often. Dried food and slobber around bowls can smell, and the floor underneath needs attention too.
  • Accidents. Clean them quickly with an enzyme-based cleaner made for pet messes. These break down the source of the smell instead of covering it up, which also helps discourage repeat visits to the same spot.
  • Fresh air. Open windows on mild DFW days and change your HVAC filters on schedule. With the AC running most of the year in North Texas, filters catch a lot of pet hair and dander.

Muddy paws and floors

North Texas storms can turn a backyard into a mud pit in an afternoon. A few habits keep that mud at the door:

  • Keep an absorbent mat at the doors your pets use most
  • Keep a towel and a small bucket or paw washer by the back door
  • Mop hard floors with a pet-safe cleaner and let them dry before pets walk on them
  • Check sliding door tracks, which collect hair, dirt and leaves quickly

Choosing pet-safe cleaning products

Pets walk on your floors, lie on your rugs and lick their paws afterward. What you clean with matters.

  • Read the labels. Look for products labeled safe for use around pets, and follow the directions for dilution and drying time.
  • Choose eco-friendly options. Gentler, eco-friendly products are a good fit for homes with curious noses.
  • Skip strong fragrances. Pets have sensitive noses. A clean home doesn't need to smell like a perfume counter.
  • Let surfaces dry. Keep pets out of freshly mopped rooms until the floor is dry.
  • Store products out of reach. Keep cleaners in closed cabinets, away from paws and mouths.
  • Ask your vet. If your pet has allergies, sensitivities or health concerns, your veterinarian is the best person to ask about specific products.

A simple pet-owner cleaning routine

Daily: scoop the litter box, wipe up spills around food and water bowls and do a quick sweep or vacuum in the busiest spots.

Weekly: vacuum all floors and furniture, wash pet bedding, mop hard floors and wipe nose prints off glass doors and windows.

Every few months: clean baseboards, vents and the corners where hair collects, and wash curtains or throws.

A deep cleaning takes care of much of that for you: spot-cleaned baseboards, dusted ceiling fans and blinds, and vacuumed upholstered furniture, right where built-up pet hair hides.
